en: Hetuduka, Dassanenapahātabbadukādi (The Dyads on Roots, the Dyads on What is to be Abandoned by Seeing, etc.)

Dependent on a state that is a root and is to be abandoned by vision, there arises a state that is not a root and is not to be abandoned by vision, by way of the root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under the root-condition there are three; under the predominance-condition there are three ... [and so on] ... under the non-disappearance-condition there are three.

Dependent on a state that is not a root and is not to be abandoned by vision, there arises a state that is not a root and is not to be abandoned by vision, by way of the root-condition. Under the root-condition there are three ... [and so on] ... under the non-disappearance-condition there are three.

Dependent on a state that is a root and is to be abandoned by cultivation, there arises a state that is not a root and is not to be abandoned by cultivation, by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under root [condition] there are three; under predominance [condition] there are three ... pe ... under non-disappearance [condition] there are three.

Dependent on a state that is not a root and is not to be abandoned by cultivation, there arises a state that is not a root and is not to be abandoned by cultivation, by way of root-condition. Under root [condition] there are three ... pe ... under non-disappearance [condition] there are three.

Dependent on a state that has a root to be abandoned by vision, there arises a state that is not a root and does not have a root to be abandoned by vision, by way of root-condition. Under root: three; under object: one ... pe ... under conascence: five ... pe ... under non-disappearance: five.

Dependent on a state that is not a root and does not have a root to be abandoned by vision, there arises a state that is not a root and does not have a root to be abandoned by vision, by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under root: one ... pe ... under non-disappearance: one.

Dependent on a state whose root is to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuka*), a state that is not a root and does not have a root to be abandoned by cultivation arises by way of the root-condition (*hetupaccaya*).
(Abbreviated. Under the root [condition], there are three; under the object [condition], one ... pe ... under the conascence [condition], five ... pe ...

Dependent on a state that is neither-rooted nor has a root to be abandoned by cultivation, there arises a state that is neither-rooted nor has a root to be abandoned by cultivation, by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under root [condition] there is one; ... pe ... under non-disappearance there is one. (Abbreviated.)
